chondroitin sulfate degradation promotes sprouting of spinal systems in injured and intact animals.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms underlying the beneficial effects of Chondroitinase treatment in spinal cord injury and the development of new treatments for spinal cord injury.
understanding the mechanisms by which the enzyme chondrotinase ABC (chABC), a potent inhibitor of chondroitin sulfate, promotes functional recovery following spinal cord injury (SCI) in rodents.
the mechanisms underlying functional recovery in the injured spinal cord and the development of new therapeutic strategies for treating spinal cord injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ChABC induced sprouting of intact and injured spinal systems after spinal cord injury is a key mechanism underlying the recovery of locomotor function.
ChABC treatment can promote sprouting within spinal cord systems that are both intact and denervated.
ChABC promotes sprouting in injured spinal systems and that this is a potential mechanism for recovery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ChABC treatment after spinal cord injury promotes sprouting of intact and injured descending spinal systems, which may underlie the functional recovery seen after ChABC treatment.
ChABC treatment promotes sprouting within the CNS and that this sprouting is a necessary component of functional recovery after spinal injury.
ChABC promotes sprouting of spinal systems and may be an important component in the mechanism underlying recovery after spinal cord and brain injury.
